clue.text: Real beano arranged, to include daughter, if back

indicators.note: something arranged has been put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged
going back means the short word just before it is read from right to left
to include something is to take it inside, so the extra letters go within the rearranged ones

blocks.note: taken as written; a beano is a British word for a party
taken as written
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: Someone organises a proper party with room for their daughter, if she comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: A beano is a jolly party in British slang; 'back' turns only the little word before it, not the whole phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Bona fide is Latin for 'in good faith' and is used to mean genuine or authentic.

clue.text: Extremely drunk, bishop on top of house

blocks.note: B is the chess notation for a bishop
house, or housey-housey, is an old British name for the game of bingo or lotto

explanation.surface: A bishop is found legless on the roof of a house.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on top of' places the first piece above the second. House is a British name for bingo, also called lotto.
explanation.definitionFit: Blotto is British slang for being completely intoxicated, too drunk to stand.

clue.text: Alliance accepting one new country

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation, a military alliance
the Roman numeral for one
N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A treaty bloc admits a newly formed state as a member.
explanation.walkthrough: NATO takes in I to make NATIO, and N follows to complete NATION.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a people or state with its own territory and government, which is what a country is.

clue.text: Female, just horrible

blocks.note: F is the standard abbreviation for female
just in the sense of fair or legitimate

explanation.surface: A woman described as simply awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Just' looks like the adverb 'merely', but here it is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Frightful and horrible are synonyms, both describing something dreadful or very unpleasant.

clue.text: Wear evening clothes round part of theatre

blocks.note: to dress, as in dressing for dinner, is to put on formal evening wear
a round shape is a circle

explanation.surface: Instructions to put on your best clothes and go round a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The dress circle is the first gallery above the stalls in a theatre, where patrons once wore evening dress.

clue.text: Heartbreaking seeing soldier trapped in overturned vehicle

indicators.note: something overturned is upside down, which in an across clue means read from right to left
something trapped in another thing is held inside it

blocks.note: a cart is a simple wheeled vehicle
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A sad scene: a soldier pinned inside a vehicle that has flipped over.
explanation.walkthrough: GI, short for 'government issue', is the usual crossword shorthand for an American soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Tragic describes something causing great sorrow, the same as heartbreaking.

clue.text: Historical object shown by RC priest inside

indicators.note: inside places the word just before it within the letters that come before that

blocks.note: taken as written: the abbreviation for Roman Catholic
Eli is the priest in the Bible who brought up Samuel, a crossword regular

explanation.surface: A Catholic priest displays a historic artefact kept inside the church.
explanation.walkthrough: ELI sits between R and C to give RELIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A relic is an object surviving from an earlier time, so it is a historical object.

clue.text: Slope that can get one treading laboriously

indicators.note: doing something laboriously suggests struggling and stumbling, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A steep hill that makes a walker plod along with effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes what a steep slope does to a walker, which makes the definition fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradient is the steepness of a slope, and by extension the incline itself.

clue.text: Tribal conflict surrounding bar raised

indicators.note: raised means lifted up, which in a down clue means the word is read from bottom to top
surrounding means going all round, so one piece wraps the other

blocks.note: a clash is a fight or conflict
an inn is a pub, a place with a bar

explanation.surface: Fighting between tribes breaks out around a pub that has been lifted up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' could be a rod or a ban, but here it stands for a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Clannish describes close loyalty to one's own clan or group, which is a tribal attitude.

clue.text: Unfashionable drink, we hear, non-member required

indicators.note: what we hear is a word judged by its sound, not its spelling

blocks.note: something unfashionable is out of fashion, or simply out
cider is a drink made from apples

explanation.surface: Someone in a bar orders a drink out of fashion as a guest who is not in the club.
explanation.walkthrough: OUT plus the sound of CIDER gives OUTSIDER.
explanation.definitionFit: An outsider is a person who does not belong to a group, the same as a non-member.

clue.text: Animal from mountain area, tailless cat

indicators.note: without a tail means the last letter of the word is cut off

blocks.note: an alp is a high mountain
A is the standard abbreviation for area
taken as written

explanation.surface: An animal from a mountain region turns out to be a cat with no tail.
explanation.walkthrough: ALP and A are followed by CAT without its last letter, giving ALPACA.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American mammal related to the llama, so it is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Fang forming part of tattoo - thug's?

indicators.note: forming part of means the letters are a piece of the words that follow

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of the first word into the start of the second

explanation.surface: A fang design making up part of a thug's tattoo.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer sits across tatTOO THug; the question mark flags that a thug might well have a fang tattooed.
explanation.definitionFit: A fang is a long pointed tooth, so the two words name the same thing.

clue.text: Pick leader in secret ballot

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, at the head of the line

blocks.note: the opening letter of secret
a ballot is a vote, an election

explanation.surface: A party chooses its leader by secret ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader' looks like the person being chosen, but it only takes the first letter of secret.
explanation.definitionFit: A selection is a choice, and pick as a noun means the same, as in 'take your pick'.

clue.text: Soldier in alien region, disorientated

indicators.note: something disorientated has lost its bearings, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A soldier stationed in a foreign land feels lost.
explanation.definitionFit: A legionnaire is a member of a legion, especially the French Foreign Legion, and so a soldier.

clue.text: Reasonable reasons to create amusement parks?

blocks.note: fair means reasonable or just
grounds are reasons, as in grounds for complaint

explanation.surface: Someone argues there are sound reasons for building theme parks.
explanation.definitionFit: Fairgrounds are open spaces with rides and stalls, which is a kind of amusement park; the question mark admits the loose match.

clue.text: Bond and nasty criminal in a state of readiness for action

definitions.text: in a state of readiness for action

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked or bent, so these letters are twisted out of order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: James Bond and a nasty villain are both poised to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' seems to describe a villain, but it signals the rearrangement of the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be on standby is to be ready to act immediately if called upon.

clue.text: One supporting that woman during a depression

indicators.note: during means within the span of something, so one piece sits inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a dent is a hollow or depression in a surface
her is the pronoun for that woman

explanation.surface: Someone props up a woman going through a bout of depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Depression' looks emotional but is a physical hollow.
explanation.definitionFit: An adherent is a follower or backer of a cause or person, someone who supports it.

clue.text: City in Brazil surrounded by outstanding lake

indicators.note: something surrounded by another thing is enclosed within it

blocks.note: super means excellent or outstanding
Rio de Janeiro, the Brazilian city

explanation.surface: A Brazilian city ringed by a splendid lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' looks like the definition, since the answer can mean much the same, but the definition is lake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lake Superior is the largest of the North American Great Lakes.

clue.text: Betray twin on trial

blocks.note: a double is an exact likeness, a twin
a cross is a trial or burden, as in a cross to bear

explanation.surface: One twin sells the other out while in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On trial' reads as a courtroom, but trial here is a burden.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-cross is to cheat someone you had agreed to cooperate with, which is to betray them.

clue.text: Foolish old man close to collapse after grabbing tail of very small wolf

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter
the close of a word is where it ends, so only its last letter is used
grabbing something means holding it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: an old coot is a silly old man
the final letter of very
the final letter of collapse

explanation.surface: A silly old man on the point of collapse after seizing a tiny wolf by the tail.
explanation.walkthrough: COOT grabs Y to make COYOT, and E comes after it. 'Very small' reads as one phrase, but very only supplies its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The coyote is a North American wild dog related to the wolf and smaller than it.

clue.text: Herb from bog by New England lake

blocks.note: a fen is low marshy ground, a bog
NE is the abbreviation for New England
L is the standard abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A herb gathered from a marsh beside a lake in New England.
explanation.definitionFit: Fennel is an aromatic plant with an aniseed flavour, used as a culinary herb.

clue.text: Holly, say, perpetually growing

blocks.note: ever means always or perpetually
green describes something growing and alive

explanation.surface: Holly keeps growing all year round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Say' marks holly as one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Holly keeps its leaves through winter, so it is an example of an evergreen plant.

clue.text: Playing organ may cause complaint

indicators.note: playing with something means fiddling with it, so these letters are moved about

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An organist's music draws grumbles from the listeners.
explanation.definitionFit: A groan is a low sound expressing displeasure, so it is a complaint.

clue.text: A flower emerged

blocks.note: taken as written
the rose is a flower

explanation.surface: A bloom appeared.
explanation.definitionFit: Arose is the past tense of arise, meaning came up or came into being, just as emerged does.

clue.text: US inventor is entertained by English university teacher

indicators.note: someone entertained by a host is taken in as a guest, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for English
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge
taken as written

explanation.surface: An American inventor is hosted by an English academic.
explanation.walkthrough: A don is a university teacher, a term used chiefly at Oxford and Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was the American inventor of the phonograph and a practical light bulb.

clue.text: Snake put away, so relax

blocks.note: to snake is to wind, as a road or river does
to down food or drink is to put it away

explanation.surface: Pack the pet snake back in its box and take it easy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Snake' looks like a noun but is the verb meaning to twist and turn.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind down is to unwind after effort, which means to relax.

clue.text: In centre of eastern country, a capital city

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle letter, the only one kept

blocks.note: the middle letter of the seven in eastern
Iran is a country in the Middle East
taken as written

explanation.surface: In the heart of an eastern land lies a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In centre of eastern country' reads like a place in the middle of Iran, but it only takes the middle letter of eastern.
explanation.definitionFit: Tirana is the capital of Albania.

clue.text: Exceedingly healthy fine

blocks.note: very means exceedingly
to be well is to be healthy

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a description of someone in excellent health, but fine is the definition as a word of agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: Very well is said to accept or agree to something, just like saying fine or all right.
